angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 11,254,339 km at 85.69 pc = 1.76 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: distance 85.69 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.057), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 85.69 +/- 4.884 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 12.5296 +/- 0.1277 mas (same row, RUWE 2.62), 98.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 16.177 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: radius 16.177 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 148.593 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.076) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 11,254,339 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5014 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: effective temperature 5014 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 8198: effective temperature 5014 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.77 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 11 published values span log g 2.43 to 2.9, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
